correctness.rationale: Starting from the exact boundary scattering equations, the common denominator has leading term \(2ik e^{-i\theta}(\varepsilon\xi-2\sin\theta)\) when \(\delta=\xi/k\). Dividing the exact amplitude numerators by this term gives \((\varepsilon-e^{i\theta})/[i(\varepsilon\xi-2\sin\theta)]\); the two vertical amplitudes have the same limit and the horizontal transmitted amplitude tends to one. Direct integration of the edge plane waves then gives the stated mass ratio. In the intermediate regime \(k|\delta|\to\infty\), the \(k^2\sin\delta\) term dominates and restores suppression. The resonance exclusion \(\varepsilon\xi\ne2\sin\theta\) is exactly where the leading denominator is nonzero.
